newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Petrol shortages add to Bulgarian crisis.
newsitem.headline: Petrol shortages add to Bulgarian crisis.

text.p: Bulgaria has added petrol shortages to its economic problems as its biggest oil refinery has no cash to pay for crude supplies, officials said on Friday.

"We receive 200 tonnes (of petrol) per day for all our service stations in the country and this volume can hardly meet the daily needs of the capital," Petar Tsanov, deputy director of the biggest state-owned fuel retailer, Petrol told, Reuters.
Tsanov said Petrol's 450 filling stations stayed open to sell mainly lubricants and sweets.
Municipalities are distributing petrol and diesel for ambulances, bread and food trucks, police, the army and for heating schools, state radio reported.
Shell Bulgaria, a Royal Dutch/Shell subsidiary and the only foreign fuel retailer in Bulgaria, said 12 of its 27 petrol stations had some kinds of fuel.
The Neftohim refinery in Bourgas is Shell's only gasoline supplier in Bulgaria. The retailer does not plan to import any gasoline for its stations as customs fees are high.
"The problem does not concern only Neftohim. It is much greater," Neftohim's marketing director Dimitar Dimitrov told the radio.
The state-owned refinery, which posted losses of 100 billion levs last year and 37 billion levs in January, has complained many times of low domestic prices.
The plant purchases its crude at international spot market prices in hard currency while domestic fuel prices are several times lower than production costs, refinery officials say.
Government price revisions cannot keep up with the fall of the lev against the dollar. The lev fell to 3,150-3,200 per dollar on the interbank maket on Friday.
Russia's state-owned Rosneft oil company said earlier this week it had reduced crude oil supplies to Neftohim because of unpaid debts.

Neftohim is delivering 1,000 tonnes of petrol and diesel per day, plant spokeswoman Tatyana Hadzhieva said by telephone. In winter months the refinery usually sells 2,500-3,000 tonnes of gasoline per day.
The plant said it has been refining only 8,000 tonnes of crude per day since Monday, while its daily capacity is 25,000.
The plant has in stock 77,000 tonnes of crude and has only one distillation unit running instead of the usual three.
Neftohim officials said they were expecting a 72,000-tonne tanker with Russian crude next week and probably one more tanker by the end of the month.
